en.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Ferromagnetism is considered as an extreme form of paramagnetism.
Statement II : The number of unpaired electrons in a Cr2+ ion (Z = 24) is the same as that of a Nd3+ ion (Z = 60).
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options below:
o: Both Statements I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statements II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statements II is true
en.sol:
Statement I is NCERT's own wording: ferromagnetism is an extreme form of paramagnetism ✓.

Statement II: Cr2+ = [Ar]3d4 → 4 unpaired electrons; Nd3+ = [Xe]4f3 → 3 unpaired. Not the same ✗.
en.hint: Write both configurations and count unpaired electrons.

en.q:
'Spin only' magnetic moment is same for which of the following ions?
A. Ti3+
B. Cr2+
C. Mn2+
D. Fe2+
E. Sc3+
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
en.sol: Unpaired electrons: Ti3+ d1 (1), Cr2+ d4 (4), Mn2+ d5 (5), Fe2+ d6 (4), Sc3+ d0 (0). Same spin-only moment (√24 = 4.90 BM): Cr2+ and Fe2+.
en.hint: Same number of unpaired electrons → same μ.

en.q: Although +3 oxidation state is most common in lanthanoids, cerium still shows +4 oxidation state because :
o: After losing one more electron, it acquires 4f<sup>14</sup> electronic configuration
Its nearest inert gas is Radon.
After losing one more electron, it acquires 4f<sup>0</sup> electronic configuration.
en.sol: Ce = [Xe]4f15d16s2. Losing four electrons gives Ce4+ = [Xe]4f0, a noble-gas configuration, which favours the +4 state (Ce4+ is a good oxidant, E° = +1.74 V).
en.hint: Ce<sup>4+</sup> has an empty 4f shell.

en.q: The stability of Cu<sup>2+</sup> is more than Cu<sup>+</sup> salts in aqueous solutions due to:
en.sol: Forming Cu2+ needs the extra second ionisation enthalpy, but Cu2+ (smaller, higher charge) has a much more negative hydration enthalpy, which more than makes up for it. So Cu2+(aq) is more stable and Cu+ disproportionates in water.
en.hint: What compensates for the second ionisation enthalpy?

en.q:
Which of the following statements are INCORRECT?
A. All the transition metals except scandium form MO oxides which are ionic.
B. The highest oxidation number corresponding to the group number in transition metal oxides is attained in Sc2O3 to Mn2O7.
C. Basic character increases from V2O3 to V2O4 to V2O5.
D. V2O4 dissolves in acids to give VO43− salts.
E. CrO is basic but Cr2O3 is amphoteric.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
en.sol:
• A ✓ (NCERT: all except Sc form ionic MO oxides).
  • B ✓ the group oxidation state is reached from Sc2O3 to Mn2O7.
  • C ✗ as the oxidation number rises (V2O3 → V2O4 → V2O5) the acidic character increases.
  • D ✗ V2O4 dissolves in acids to give VO2+ salts (V2O5 gives VO43− in alkali).
  • E ✓

Incorrect: C and D.
en.hint: Higher oxidation state → more acidic oxide.

en.q: Zr (Z = 40) and Hf (Z = 72) have similar atomic and ionic radii because of :
en.sol: Between Zr (period 5) and Hf (period 6) come the 14 lanthanoids. The poor shielding by 4f electrons causes the lanthanoid contraction, which cancels the expected size increase, so Zr (160 pm) and Hf (159 pm) are almost the same size.
en.hint: What lies between period 5 and period 6 of group 4?

hi.q: Zr (Z = 40) और Hf (Z = 72) की परमाणु और आयनिक त्रिज्याएँ समान हैं, इसका कारण है :

hi.sol: Zr (आवर्त 5) और Hf (आवर्त 6) के बीच 14 लैन्थेनॉयड आते हैं। 4f इलेक्ट्रॉनों के दुर्बल परिरक्षण से लैन्थेनॉयड आकुंचन होता है, जो अपेक्षित आकार वृद्धि को निरस्त कर देता है, अतः Zr (160 pm) और Hf (159 pm) लगभग समान आकार के हैं।
hi.hint: वर्ग 4 के आवर्त 5 और आवर्त 6 के बीच क्या आता है?

en.q: Zr (4d series) and Hf (5d series) have almost identical radii (160 pm and 159 pm) and very similar properties. This is because of:
o: the lanthanoid contraction, caused by the imperfect shielding of 4f electrons filled before the 5d series
en.sol: NCERT 4.3.2: in a transition series the radii decrease slowly with increasing atomic number, because the new electron enters a d orbital and shields the outer electrons poorly. From the 3d to the 4d series the size increases as expected, but the 5d radii are virtually the same as the 4d ones. This is because the 4f orbitals are filled before the 5d series begins; 4f electrons shield poorly, so the steady decrease in size across the lanthanoids (lanthanoid contraction) exactly compensates the expected increase. Hence Zr and Hf are nearly identical in size and occur together in nature.
en.hint: Fourteen 4f elements sit between them.

en.q: Transition metals readily form alloys with each other mainly because:
o: their atomic radii are similar (within about 15%) and their characteristics are similar, so one metal's atoms can replace another's in the lattice
they all have the same atomic number
en.sol: NCERT 4.3.14: an alloy is a blend of metals prepared by mixing the components; it may be a homogeneous solid solution in which atoms of one metal are distributed randomly among atoms of the other. Such alloys form between atoms whose metallic radii are within about 15% of each other. Because of similar radii and other characteristics, transition metals readily form alloys, which are hard and often have high melting points. Ferrous alloys are the best known (Cr, V, W, Mo and Mn in steels and stainless steel). Alloys of transition with non-transition metals, such as brass (Cu–Zn) and bronze (Cu–Sn), are also industrially important.
en.hint: Similar-sized atoms swap places easily.

en.q: Among the oxides of manganese, as the oxidation state of the metal increases from MnO to Mn<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub>:

en.q: Which statement about the lanthanoids is incorrect?
o: The common oxidation state is +3; Ce also shows +4, and Eu and Yb also show +2.
Their atomic and ionic radii increase steadily from La to Lu.
They are silvery white, soft metals that tarnish rapidly in air.

en.sol: NCERT 4.5: the fourteen elements after lanthanum (Ce to Lu) are the lanthanoids; they resemble one another closely. +3 is the principal oxidation state; Ce4+ (favoured by its noble gas configuration) is a strong oxidant, Eu2+ and Yb2+ (f7 and f14) also exist. The atomic and ionic (M3+) radii decrease steadily from La to Lu: the lanthanoid contraction, due to imperfect shielding of one 4f electron by another. They are silvery white soft metals that tarnish rapidly in air; hardness increases with atomic number.
en.hint: Contraction means getting smaller.

en.q: The actinoids show a wider range of oxidation states than the lanthanoids mainly because:
o: the 5f, 6d and 7s levels have comparable energies, so more electrons can take part in bonding
they have fewer electrons than the lanthanoids
their 5f orbitals are buried deeper than 4f orbitals
they do not have any f electrons
en.sol: NCERT 4.6.1: all actinoids have 7s2 with variable occupancy of 5f and 6d. The 5f orbitals resemble 4f in angular shape but are not as buried, so 5f electrons can participate in bonding to a greater extent. Because the 5f, 6d and 7s levels are of comparable energies, the actinoids show a greater range of oxidation states (for example U +3 to +6, Np and Pu up to +7). Irregularities in configuration are related to the stability of f0, f7 and f14.
en.hint: Energies close together → more electrons available.
